🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Dos Bocas Output Up 12.7% Year-on-Year</u>

Pemex's Olmeca refinery at Dos Bocas averaged 215,000 barrels per day of fuels in September, up 12.7% from 192,000 a year earlier, La Jornada reports. It's the refinery's third straight month above 200,000 bpd, after an August record of 270,000, and it now supplies more than a fifth of Pemex's 1.029 million bpd of fuel output. The plant they swore would never refine a drop.

🇲🇽🎨 "Education transforms people's lives, but above all it transforms the life of nations. When there is education, peace is built. When there is education, a future is built." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas Handing out Gertrudis Bocanegra university scholarship cards at the Universidad Politécnica de Chiapas, she asked students whether education is only for personal benefit "or to put it also at the service of others." "Always think that this school was made by the people of Mexico," and the scholarship is given "by the people of Chiapas and the people of Mexico." What they do with it is up to them: "whether you dedicate yourselves exclusively to your own person, or build a different future." Student Sofía Castañeda, who travels about two hours each way to class, said what often decides whether students keep studying "is whether we have the bus fare or not."

🇲🇽🎨 "In that Constitution it was said, from back then, that the sovereignty of our homeland did not lie in a few, but resided in the people of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas Speaking to engineering students in Suchiapa on November 7, she contrasted Mexico's independence with the rest of Latin America, where it was led by criollo officers of the viceroyalty's army who wanted a country "for themselves." In Mexico it was led by a village priest, Hidalgo, who cried out for independence on September 16 and soon after called for the abolition of slavery, and by his disciple Morelos, who took up the fight after Hidalgo was executed and wrote the Apatzingán Constitution, the basis of the 1917 Constitution: the same education "for the son of the hacendado as for the son of the peon," and "moderate indigence and opulence."

🇲🇽✊ "This is the Mexico you got to live in. Be part of history. Don't stay away. Don't watch it go by from your window. Be part of this enormous transformation our country is living. And if you see an injustice, raise your voice, in whatever way you decide." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas Closing the scholarship event, she ran through the heroines and heroes "unique in the history of the world": Josefa Ortiz Téllez Girón ("because women don't belong to anyone, we don't belong to the husband we marry"), and Leona Vicario, who answered a conservador who said she joined independence only to follow her husband: "We women love our family, we love our children, but we have the right and the obligation to fight for our homeland." Benito Juárez, Villa, Zapata, Madero, and Chiapas's own Belisario Domínguez, "who raised his voice to say long live freedom of expression." "Like Mexico, there is no other."
banner: "IF YOU SEE AN INJUSTICE, RAISE YOUR VOICE"
